title: Guillermo Rauch on saying no, picking battles, and designing products for the AI era
summary: Vercel's CEO explains why great companies are defined by what they reject, how a high quality bar can coexist with speed, and why product simplicity depends on stage. He also covers hiring on tangible output and why AI interfaces often need more UI, not less.

principles.text: Great companies are defined by how many attractive ideas they reject before shipping the one that earns a place in the lineup.
principles.quote: what makes a company good is how much they reject over time how many things they say no to how many attract seemingly attractive on the surface ideas they rule out before they say yes

principles.text: Pick your battles. Being right beats being first, and this matters more as a company matures.
principles.quote: you don't always have to be first you have to be right and and that's what I think companies over time optimize more around how do you pick your battles

principles.text: A high bar isn't slow. Shrink the blast radius of experiments so you ship broadly only with strong evidence.
principles.quote: you can find the ways of reducing the blast radius of your experimentation such that when it's the time that you bring the product to everybody you've accumulated enough evidence of success

principles.text: Product simplicity is stage-dependent. What works from zero to one won't work from one to two or later.
principles.quote: the Simplicity of your product from zero to one might not be the Simplicity of your product from one to two and two to three

principles.text: Hire on tangible output. Look at what candidates have shipped and shared, not just brand-name resumes.
principles.quote: what are they putting out into the world that is tangible what can I use what what hyperlinks Have you shared with the World by your creations

principles.text: AI products are probabilistic, so good AI interfaces often give users more choices and UI, not less.
principles.quote: it's actually giving you more UI not less because it's uncertain about what it is that you actually want so it needs to give you more choices
